subject: CloudMarket marketplace: geo-routing, retention & deletion SLA — Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <erossi@cloudmarket.co>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.inference>
Cc: CloudMarket Procurement <procure@cloudmarket.co>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing: residency / retention / deletion questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the call this morning — quick follow-up from CloudMarket's Marketplace team. We have three items our legal and platform teams want clarified before we finalize the listing: 

1) Region-level routing: can Redwood guarantee that all inference requests and associated customer data (including prompt text, returned tokens, and any generated metadata) for a given CloudMarket account can be pinned to a specific cloud region (e.g., us-east-1, europe-west1, eastus) when deployed through the Marketplace? We need to understand if routing is at the account, model, or request level.

2) Retention defaults and options: what are default retention periods for (a) raw request/response logs, (b) audit/tracing logs, and (c) model telemetry? Can we set custom retention per-account through an MSA addendum?

3) Deletion timelines / proof: if a customer requests deletion, what is the end-to-end timeline (hub -> cache -> backups) and what proof can Redwood provide (signed log entries, drive links to deletion audit)?

Can you send a short Q&A doc and any region-mapping sheet we can attach to the Marketplace listing? Procurement also wants to confirm whether retention SLAs differ across AWS/GCP/Azure offerings.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Product Partnerships
CloudMarket

Elena — thanks for laying these out. Below is a concise Q&A; I'll attach our resident FAQ and a region mapping CSV. If you want, Vanessa can propose contract language for the MSA addendum.

Q1 — Region-level routing
- Short answer: Yes, we support account-level pinning to a region when deployed via Redwood Private/Dedicated; for hosted Marketplace deployments we support policy-based routing.
- Details:
  - Account-level pinning: available for Dedicated and Private (VPC) deployments. When enabled, all inference traffic and derived artifacts (request/response logs, KV cache entries, generated embeddings) are constrained to the selected region's infrastructure and object stores (S3/GCS/Blob).
  - Policy-based routing (hosted): you can set a policy that routes by account or by request header (x-region-preference). If capacity requires fallback, we will route to the nearest compatible region and record the event in the audit log; fallback behavior is configurable via rollout policy (e.g., strict -> reject, permissive -> fallback).
  - Implementation notes: we store object artifacts in the native cloud object store for that region (S3 for AWS, GCS for GCP, Blob for Azure) and our metadata service marks items with region tags.

Q2 — Retention defaults and custom settings
- Defaults (hosted): request/response logs = 30 days; audit/tracing logs = 90 days; model telemetry (performance/latency metrics) = 365 days.
- Dedicated/Private: retention defaults can be adjusted per-account; we support customer-managed retention via configuration in the Console or via API.
- Per-account custom retention: yes — addendum language can specify min/max ranges and whether logs are stored by Redwood or exported to a customer-owned bucket for longer-term retention.

Q3 — Deletion timelines and proof
- Typical end-to-end deletion timeline (hosted):
  1) Deletion request received -> mark records for deletion: immediate (0–5 minutes)
  2) Primary object store deletion (S3/GCS/Blob): async job within 1–24 hours depending on object size and batching
  3) KV cache / in-memory caches: evicted immediately; snapshots removed within 1 hour
  4) Backups / long-term snapshots: purged on the next snapshot retention cycle (configurable; typical max 30 days)
- Proof: we provide a deletion audit bundle (signed JSON lines) containing resource IDs, deletion timestamps, node IDs, and checksums. For Marketplace customers we can surface a Drive link to the audit bundle or include it in the Portal as a signed artifact.

Cross-cloud consistency
- We maintain the same retention primitives across AWS/GCP/Azure. Differences to note:
  - Storage behavior (e.g., object lifecycle policies) is implemented using the cloud-native APIs — retention enforcement is orchestrated by Redwood but deletion semantics follow the provider's guarantees (e.g., eventual object removal in S3).
  - Network egress, routing, and region naming conventions vary; we translate CloudMarket region aliases into provider regions via the attached mapping sheet.

Attachments: redwood_data_residency_faq_v3.pdf, region-mapping-sheet.csv (attached)

Next steps: Vanessa will draft a short MSA addendum clause (retention, strict region pinning, deletion audit). Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync this week to confirm exact region mappings and whether you want exported logs to a customer-owned bucket?

Elena — copying Marissa from Product as she owns Marketplace integration requirements. A few legal/contract notes and suggested language you can drop into the MSA addendum: 

1) Region pinning clause (suggested): 
"Redwood will, at Customer's election, provision and serve Customer data and associated inference artifacts from a single cloud region (the 'Designated Region') supported by the Redwood Marketplace offering. Redwood shall not intentionally route Customer data outside the Designated Region except for (a) customer-requested exports, (b) emergency failover as documented in the Service Resilience Policy, or (c) as required by law. Any permitted failover events will be recorded in the Deletion & Routing Audit Bundle."

2) Retention & deletion SLA (suggested):
"Redwood will honor deletion requests with a completion window not to exceed 30 days for primary stores and 45 days for archived snapshots, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Upon completion Redwood will provide a signed deletion audit bundle within 72 hours."

3) Export option: we recommend an option where logs are periodically exported to a customer-owned cloud bucket (S3/GCS/Blob) to meet longer retention or residency constraints. Export schedules can be daily/hourly and are configurable per-account.

Marissa — happy to work with Product to create a short Marketplace FAQ card (2–3 bullets) that appears on the listing describing region pinning and deletion proof.

Elena — happy to propose exact clause text for procurement and shepherd through redlines.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
